name: NORTH KOREA

flag.title: Flag of N. Korea
flag.note: Red star on white disc, broad red band

lead: North Korea is the northern half of a peninsula between China and Japan. It is one of the most secretive countries on Earth. The Kim family has ruled it since 1948. The sacred volcano Paektu rises on the Chinese border.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: About 80% of North Korea is mountains. The Nangnim and Hamgyong ranges run down it like a spine. The Yalu and Tumen rivers mark its borders with China and Russia.
Mount Paektu in the far north is a sleeping volcano with a crater lake called Heaven Lake. The lake is 384 m deep. Summit winters can plunge to −48 °C.
animals: The Asiatic black bear lives in the cold northern forests. A white crescent on its chest earns it the name moon bear. In autumn it raids fruit trees.
The Korean water deer lives in river marshes. Males have no antlers. Instead they grow long curved fangs below the lip. People call it the 'vampire deer'.
culture: Every year the Mass Games fill Pyongyang's May Day Stadium, the world's biggest. Over 100,000 performers move in perfect unison. Guinness calls it the largest gymnastic display on Earth.
Schoolchildren spend hundreds of hours studying the ruling Kim family. Citizens once had to pick a hairstyle from just 28 government-approved cuts.
history: Korea was one kingdom for over a thousand years. Japan took control in 1910. After 1945, the Soviet Union backed the North and the United States backed the South.
The Korean War (1950–53) ended in a ceasefire, not a peace treaty. So the two Koreas are still at war. Kim Jong Un has led since 2011.
wows: North Korea ditched its own Juche calendar in 2024.
Pyongyang's 105-storey Ryugyong Hotel has stood since 1987 but never opened.
Mount Paektu's AD 946 eruption sent ash to Japan.
Clocks moved 30 minutes in 2015, then back in 2018.
30,000 schoolchildren make the world's biggest live mosaic with cards.
North Korea has its own internet, Kwangmyong.
The DMZ, undisturbed for 70+ years, is now a wildlife sanctuary.

myths.myth: North and South Korea speak different languages
myths.fact: Both speak Korean. Only some words and accents differ, like British and American English.

myths.myth: Bears sleep so deeply in winter that nothing wakes them
myths.fact: Bears sleep lightly and wake easily. Mother bears even give birth during their winter sleep.
